newsitem.title: USA: US gold coins sales increase sharply in July - CPM.
newsitem.headline: US gold coins sales increase sharply in July - CPM.

text.p: Gold coin sales increased sharply in July in North America and Asia, fueled by bargain hunting and the perception that gold prices may have reached a cyclical low, New York based industry consultants CPM Group said.
Sales of the U.S. Mint's gold Eagle coins jumped to 77,000 ounces, up from 31,500 ounces in June and 18,500 ounces in July last year.
This was the highest monthly sales figure since January 1991, when demand reached 98,000 ounces.
The spot price of gold fell to 12-year lows around $315.00 an ounce in early July this year.
In the first seven months of 1997 gold Eagle sales totalled 369,750 ounces, up 165 percent from 139,500 ounces in the same period in 1996.
Demand for the Royal Canadian Mint's gold Maple Leaf rose at even faster pace, according to coin dealers, although specific figures have not been made public.
Rising sales were also reported for a variety of other bullion coins in the first half of 1997.
Lower silver prices also sparked demand for the U.S. Mint's silver Eagle coins, CPM Group said.
Sales of the silver Eagle rose to 305,000 ounce in July, up from 220,000 ounces in June and 75,000 ounces in July last year.
In the first seven months of 1997, silver Eagle sales amounted to 2,046,000 ounces, up 94 percent from 1,053,000 ounces in the similar period last year.
The spot price of silver fell to a three year low around $4.17 an ounce in early July.

Under the U.S. tax bill recently signed into law by President Clinton, U.S. investors now will be able to add silver and platinum coins to their Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs), as well as gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion.
Investors were already allowed to add American Eagle gold coins to their IRAs. However, precious metals investments still are subject to a higher capital gains tax than equities or bonds.
